research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK Planning Inspectorate, Natural England, DfT and Planning Data verification; 2026 currentness where present, definitive-map/order status, highway stopping-up, common-land consent/deregistration, village-green registration, NO_DATA provenance, exact-geometry and cross-regime fail-closed gates. Not parcel-level accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Public rights of way: local highway authority responsibilities
official_sources.fact: Highway authorities must maintain the definitive map and statement and protect recorded public rights of way.
official_sources.gate: A local-authority map or route display is not by itself proof of exact current legal alignment, width, status or absence of pending modification orders.

official_sources.name: Definitive maps of public rights of way: change the legal records
official_sources.fact: Natural England guidance describes definitive maps as legal records and explains creation, diversion and closure procedures.
official_sources.gate: A proposed, claimed or observed route is not the legal definitive route unless the definitive map/statement and live orders are checked.

official_sources.name: Public rights of way: landowner responsibilities
official_sources.fact: Landowners must not obstruct public rights of way and changes require the appropriate highway-authority process.
official_sources.gate: Landowner control, fencing or an informal alternative route does not extinguish or legally divert a public right of way.

official_sources.name: Rights of way guidance booklet
official_sources.fact: Planning Inspectorate guidance updated 22 April 2026 covers objections to definitive-map and public-path orders.
official_sources.gate: An objection, hearing or inspector process is procedural evidence only; the confirmed order and map determine the legal change.

official_sources.name: Object to a public right of way order
official_sources.fact: PINS explains that councils can confirm unopposed orders, while opposed orders may be referred to the Inspectorate.
official_sources.gate: An advertised or opposed order is not a confirmed legal change until the competent authority or Inspectorate confirms it.

official_sources.name: Rights of way decisions and maps published in 2026
official_sources.fact: PINS publishes 2026 rights-of-way decisions and maps with decision dates and authority/case references.
official_sources.gate: A national decisions index is discovery evidence; exact parcel effect requires the specific order, map, decision and effective status.

official_sources.name: Rights of way notices and rejection letters published in 2026
official_sources.fact: PINS publishes 2026 start-date, hearing, inquiry and rejection material for rights-of-way orders.
official_sources.gate: A start notice, hearing notice or rejection letter must not be treated as a confirmed route change or final parcel status.

official_sources.name: All rights of way order published case documents 2015-present
official_sources.fact: The PINS collection links order notices, decisions and maps from 2015 to the present.
official_sources.gate: A collection entry is an index, not proof that a particular order applies to a target parcel or remains operative.

official_sources.name: Schedule 14 Direction Guidance
official_sources.fact: Applicants can seek a Secretary of State direction if a definitive-map modification application has not been decided within 12 months.
official_sources.gate: A Schedule 14 direction concerns authority timing; it does not decide the underlying right-of-way claim or modify the definitive map.

official_sources.name: Schedule 14 direction application
official_sources.fact: PINS publishes the route for applying for a Schedule 14 direction after a 12-month decision delay.
official_sources.gate: Submitting or receiving a direction request is not evidence that the claimed route exists or will be added to the definitive map.

official_sources.name: Local authority rights of way improvement plans
official_sources.fact: Authorities must review rights-of-way improvement plans and assess network condition, accessibility and opportunities.
official_sources.gate: A rights-of-way improvement plan is strategic planning evidence, not a legal definitive-map change or guaranteed infrastructure delivery.

official_sources.name: How to apply to close or divert a highway
official_sources.fact: DfT guidance covers stopping-up and diversion under sections 247, 248 and 253 of the Town and Country Planning Act.
official_sources.gate: Planning permission alone does not remove highway rights; the stopping-up/diversion order must be separately made and effective.

official_sources.name: Apply to close or divert a highway
official_sources.fact: DfT requires plans plus planning permission or application evidence for stopping-up applications.
official_sources.gate: An application package or submitted plan is not a made order and does not itself extinguish highway rights.

official_sources.name: Stopping up orders
official_sources.fact: DfT distinguishes sections 247, 248, 249 and 253 and their different purposes.
official_sources.gate: A section number or draft order route must not be treated as proof of legal closure, pedestrianisation or access removal.

official_sources.name: National transport casework team
official_sources.fact: The National Transport Casework team handles section 249 pedestrianisation and section 251 removal of rights over land held for planning purposes.
official_sources.gate: Casework eligibility or processing does not prove that vehicle or public rights have been removed; the relevant order and conditions must be verified.

official_sources.name: Works on Common land and Deregistering Common Land: guidance
official_sources.fact: PINS consolidates Section 38 works guidance and Section 16 deregistration/exchange guidance, including 2026 updates.
official_sources.gate: A common-land guidance collection is not parcel registration evidence, consent, deregistration or planning permission.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 1a
official_sources.fact: Section 38 consent may be required for restricted works on registered common land and does not grant other permissions.
official_sources.gate: Section 38 consent is not planning permission, landowner consent or clearance under other legal regimes.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 1b
official_sources.fact: The March 2026 guidance identifies works/processes considered outside Section 38 where access is not prevented or impeded, subject to context.
official_sources.gate: A 'no Section 38 consent' conclusion is not a blanket permission and may still be legally contestable or require other approvals.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 2b: Works on Town & Village Greens
official_sources.fact: PINS explains statutory protection for town and village greens and special consent considerations.
official_sources.gate: Village-green status or a map label is not permission for works; exact registration, ownership, rights and applicable legislation must be checked.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 2c
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 23 March 2026 explains commons governed by schemes of management or local legislation.
official_sources.gate: A scheme common may have bespoke powers and consents; generic Section 38 assumptions must not replace the actual scheme or local Act.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 3: inquiries and hearings
official_sources.fact: PINS guidance describes inquiry/hearing procedures for common-land works and deregistration applications.
official_sources.gate: A hearing, inquiry or site visit is procedural status only and does not imply consent or refusal.

official_sources.name: Common Land Guidance Sheet 4: resurfacing
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 23 March 2026 distinguishes hard resurfacing, repairs and loose-surface works on common land.
official_sources.gate: Surface type and access effects must be checked exactly; generic road/track presence does not determine whether consent is required.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 5
official_sources.fact: PINS distinguishes maintenance of lawful existing works from extensions and historical/unlawful works.
official_sources.gate: Existing physical works are not proof of lawful consent, and maintenance rights do not automatically authorise extensions.

official_sources.name: Common Land Guidance Sheet 6
official_sources.fact: Section 38 consents can carry precise modifications, conditions, access requirements and time limits.
official_sources.gate: A consent cannot be treated as unrestricted or permanent without reading its exact conditions and duration.

official_sources.name: Common Land Guidance Sheet 7
official_sources.fact: PINS explains applications to vary or revoke modifications/conditions and the three-month route under section 39(5).
official_sources.gate: A variation request does not alter the consent unless and until a decision varying or revoking the condition is made.

official_sources.name: Common Land Guidance Sheet 9
official_sources.fact: Guidance explains statutory exemptions under section 38(6), including some enactment-authorised works and electronic communications apparatus.
official_sources.gate: An exemption from Section 38 is not exemption from planning, highway, environmental, ownership or other legal controls.

official_sources.name: Common land guidance sheet 10: highways and cattle grids
official_sources.fact: Guidance distinguishes Section 38 common-land consent from Highways Act cattle-grid approval and public-right-of-way protections.
official_sources.gate: A highway/common overlap requires regime-specific checks; one consent does not automatically authorise interference with another right.

official_sources.name: Common Land Guidance Sheet 11
official_sources.fact: Section 38 consent does not authorise interference with a public right of way and highway-authority powers remain relevant.
official_sources.gate: Common-land consent must not be promoted to authority to obstruct, gate or divert a public right of way.

official_sources.name: Common Land Guidance Sheet 12
official_sources.fact: Guidance explains Section 41 county-court enforcement for certain unauthorised works and the limits of Inspectorate/registration-authority duties.
official_sources.gate: A complaint or allegation of unlawful works is not proof of illegality or a court order; exact consent and enforcement status must be checked.

official_sources.name: Application form for consent to construct works on common land
official_sources.fact: PINS publishes the application form and notes for Section 38 and related common-land consent routes.
official_sources.gate: Submitting a form is not consent, and the form does not replace planning permission, landowner agreement or other statutory approvals.

official_sources.name: Notes on deregistering or exchanging common land or greens
official_sources.fact: Notes updated 16 February 2026 explain Section 16 release/replacement land, access, designations, consultation and mapping.
official_sources.gate: A Section 16 application or proposed replacement land does not deregister the common/green until a decision is made and implemented.

official_sources.name: Common land notices and decisions 2023-2026
official_sources.fact: PINS common-land decision register was updated 6 July 2026 with current hearings and decisions.
official_sources.gate: A national case register is discovery evidence; exact legal effect requires the individual decision, plans and parcel relationship.

official_sources.name: Manage your town and village greens
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK explains restrictions on damaging/interfering works and the deregistration/replacement-land route for greens.
official_sources.gate: Ownership or proposed works do not override green protections, and deregistration or planning approval must be verified separately.

official_sources.name: Town and village greens: how to register
official_sources.fact: Defra guidance explains registration criteria and trigger/terminating events affecting the right to apply.
official_sources.gate: Historic recreational use or an application does not establish registered green status; the register and live application/trigger status must be checked.

official_sources.name: Application for registration of land as a town or village green
official_sources.fact: Defra provides Form 44 for applications to register land as a town or village green.
official_sources.gate: An application form or submitted claim is not a completed registration and does not itself create final green status.

official_sources.name: Planning Data common land and village green dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 records, 0 providers and no collection attempt, with MHCLG-created provenance pending authoritative data.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform rows means NO_DATA and must not be interpreted as absence of common land or village-green constraints.

official_sources.name: Planning Data common land and village greens consideration
official_sources.fact: Planning Data marks the consideration as a design-stage backlog with unknown record counts/update frequency and no technical specification.
official_sources.gate: A backlog consideration is not an operational authoritative dataset and cannot support parcel-level absence or presence conclusions.
